*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

nextion_id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The ID of the Nextion display.

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

variable_name.docs:
**string**: The name of the Nextion variable. Any value over `0`   is considered to be **on**

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

visible.docs:
**boolean**: Visible or not

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

component_id.docs:
**string**: The ID (the number, not name!) of the component to track.

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

page_id.docs:
**string**: The ID of the page the component is on. Use `0`   for the default page.

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

update_interval.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: The duration to update the sensor. If using a [Nextion Custom Binary Sensor Protocol](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#nextion-custom-binary-sensor-protocol) this should not be used

*See also: [Nextion Binary Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

set_brightness.docs: You can use this [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#actions-action) to set the brightness of the Nextion's backlight.

auto_wake_on_touch.docs:
**boolean**: If set to `true`, the Nextion will be configured to wake from sleep when touched.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

brightness.docs:
**percentage**: When specified, the display brightness will be set to this value at boot.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

command_spacing.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: Sets the minimum time between commands sent to the Nextion display. A higher value can help prevent buffer overflows but will result in slower interface updates. Range is `0-255ms`. Defaults to `0ms` (disabled).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

exit_reparse_on_start.docs:
**boolean**: Request the Nextion exit Active Reparse Mode before setup of the display. Defaults to `false`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

max_commands_per_loop.docs:
**integer**: Limits the number of commands processed per loop cycle. This helps prevent stack overflows when a large number of commands are queued. Lower values (for example, `20`  ) may help improve stability in constrained environments.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

max_queue_age.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: Maximum age in milliseconds for queued commands before they are automatically removed. This helps prevent stale commands from being executed after delays. Set to ``0`` to disable age-based removal (commands are only limited by queue size). **Note:** Very low values (e.g., \<50ms) may cause commands to be dropped before transmission due to ESPHome's loop timing (~16ms). Recommended minimum is 100ms when enabled. Range: 0-65535. Defaults to ``8000`` (8 seconds).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

max_queue_size.docs:
**integer**: Sets the maximum number of commands that can be queued at once. When the limit is reached, new commands will be dropped and a warning will be logged. This helps prevent memory overflows or boot-time crashes in complex setups that issue a large number of commands in rapid succession. If not set, the queue size is unlimited.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_buffer_overflow.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed when the Nextion reports a buffer overflow. See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_buffer_overflow).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_page.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed after a page change. See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_page).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_setup.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed after ESPHome connects to the Nextion. See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_setup).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_sleep.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed when the Nextion goes to sleep. See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_sleep).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_touch.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed after a touch event (press or release). See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_touch).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

on_wake.docs:
**[Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions)**: An action to be performed when the Nextion wakes up. See [Nextion Automation](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion-on_sleep).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

skip_connection_handshake.docs:
**boolean**: Sets whether the initial display connection handshake process is skipped. When set to `true`, the connection will be established without performing the handshake. This can be useful when using Nextion Simulator. Defaults to `false`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

start_up_page.docs:
**int**: Sets the page to display when ESPHome connects to the Nextion. (Nextion shows page 0 on start-up by default).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

startup_override_ms.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: Time in milliseconds to wait before forcing the display to be marked as ready if it hasn't responded to the connection handshake. Set to ``0`` to disable the override and wait indefinitely for the handshake. This is useful for displays with slower startup sequences or to enforce strict handshake requirements. Range: 0-65535. Defaults to ``8000`` (8 seconds).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

tft_upload_http_retries.docs:
**int**: Number of retries for transient HTTP failures during TFT upload. On Arduino, this applies to the initial connection request. On ESP-IDF, this applies to chunk read operations. Range: 1-255. Defaults to `5`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

tft_upload_http_timeout.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: HTTP request timeout for TFT upload transfers. Applies to each individual HTTP request during the upload process. Range: 1-65535ms. Defaults to `4.5s`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

tft_upload_watchdog_timeout.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: Temporarily adjusts the system watchdog timeout for the duration of the TFT transfer process. The original timeout is automatically restored when the transfer completes (whether successful or not). May be useful on slow connections or when transferring large TFT files. Do not set this unless you are experiencing device reboots due to watchdog timeouts during TFT uploads; doing so may prevent the device from rebooting due to a legitimate problem. Only available on ESP32.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

tft_url.docs:
**string**: The URL from which to download the TFT file for display firmware updates (Nextion OTA). See [Nextion Upload](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion_upload_tft).

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

touch_sleep_timeout.docs:
**int**: Sets internal No-touch-then-sleep timer in seconds. Range: 0 (disabled) or 3-65535 seconds (max: ~18 hours). Values 1-2 are auto-corrected to 3. When set, Nextion will automatically enter sleep mode after the specified period of no touch activity. This setting persists until device reboot or reset. Note: The display will only wake up by restart or by configuring `auto_wake_on_touch: true`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

uart_id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The ID of the [UART Bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart) you wish to use for this display. Specify this when you have multiple UART configurations.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

update_interval.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: The interval to call the lambda to update the display. Defaults to `5s`.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

wake_up_page.docs:
**int**: Sets the page to display after waking up

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

lambda.docs:
**[lambda](https://esphome.io/automations/templates#config-lambda)**: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the Nextion display. See [Rendering Lambda](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#display-nextion_lambda) for more information. This is typically empty. The individual components for the Nextion will handle almost all functions needed for updating display elements.

*See also: [Nextion TFT LCD Display](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#configuration-variables)*

publish.docs: You can also publish a state to a Nextion sensor from elsewhere in your YAML file with the `sensor.nextion.publish` action.

precision.docs:
**int**: This is for Nextion float components. This sets the precision that the component is set to. This typically is the `vvs1` setting of the component.

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

update_interval.docs:
**[Time](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#time)**: The duration to update the sensor. This typically should be set for waveforms to send periodic updates.

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

wave_channel_id.docs:
**int**: The waveform ID in a range of 0-3

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

wave_max_length.docs:
**int**: How many data points to store. Typically this is the width of the component in the Nextion

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

wave_max_value.docs:
**int**: The max value. Set `dis` to the height of the component in the Nextion editor and this to the max value that will be sent. This will set up the proper scaling.

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*

waveform_send_last_value.docs:
**int**: This will send the last value set during an update interval. Setting to true will give a timeseries style graph

*See also: [Nextion Sensor Component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/nextion#configuration-variables)*
